Unrestricted sandwich robustness value for loss of significance

rv_sand.Rd

Computes lower and upper bounds on the weakest added scalar index that removes significance under the specified sandwich rule. Strength is the maximum of treatment-side and outcome-side partial R-squared.

Usage

rv_sand(model, treatment = NULL, vcov = "HC1", cluster = NULL,
  alpha = 0.05, critical = NULL, null = 0, n_starts = 8L,
  max_iterations = 80L, seed = 1234L, tolerance = 5e-8,
  max_radius = 1 - 1e-6, search_steps = 12L, run_search = TRUE,
  supplied_witnesses = list())

Arguments

model

An unweighted full-rank lm model with an intercept, or an rv_cache.

treatment

Name of one target model-matrix column; required for lm.

vcov

HC0/HC1, one-way CR0/CR1, HAC_Bartlett_L4, HAC_QS_BW5, TWCR0_raw, TWCR1_raw, or a fixed covariance rule.

cluster

One- or two-way cluster labels aligned with rows retained by the fit, or a formula evaluated in its model frame.

alpha

Two-sided significance level.

critical

Optional fixed positive cutoff. Defaults to a t cutoff with augmented residual degrees of freedom for HC/HAC, number of clusters minus one for one-way CR, and min(G1,G2)-1 for two-way CR.

null

Null value of the target coefficient.

n_starts

Number of screened residual directions.

max_iterations

Maximum local optimizer iterations.

seed

Local random seed, leaving the caller's RNG state unchanged.

tolerance

Positive numerical refit and interval-closing tolerance, at most 0.001.

max_radius

Largest strength queried by the radial search; strictly between zero and one. A previously verified witness above this value may still be retained.

search_steps

Number of radial queries.

run_search

Run fallback search after direct checks.

supplied_witnesses

Vectors or result objects; each candidate is independently rechecked.

Details

An analytical continuous score envelope supplies the lower bound. Failed local searches never increase this bound. Every finite upper bound is the measured strength of an actual index verified by a full augmented QR regression. A point value is returned only when the verified bounds agree within tolerance. The bounds are computational intervals, not confidence intervals or formal interval arithmetic.

The observed test and cutoff are held fixed. If the observed test already does not reject (absolute t no greater than the cutoff), the loss RV is zero by convention. Boundary attainment and strict loss are recorded separately. The current implementation supports unweighted OLS with HC0/HC1, one-way CR0/CR1, raw two-way CR0/CR1, and fixed Bartlett or quadratic-spectral HAC. Weights and order stay fixed; adaptive tuning and PSD repair are not performed. Nonpositive candidate variances are inadmissible. See fixed_hac_rule for rule constructors and article aliases.

Value

A robust_rv_result: RV_lower, RV_upper, rv (missing unless resolved), status, tolerances, runtime, and the independently refitted best_witness_z. A missing upper bound means that no admissible loss index was found; it does not establish infeasibility.

See also

rv_cal, sandwich_rv

Examples

fit <- lm(mpg ~ wt + hp + disp, data = mtcars)
rv_sand(fit, "wt", run_search = FALSE)
#> RV_sand 
#>   Covariance: HC1 
#>   Baseline decision: reject 
#>   Status: LOWER_BOUND_ONLY / sand 
#>   Certificate: analytical_lower_bound_only 
#>   Certified lower bound: 0.02032113 
#>   Certified upper bound: not found 
#>   Runtime: 0.002 seconds
